background_notes.justification: The time coordinate is continuous, so the inverse image of (0,∞) is open. A neighborhood of z is contained in Ω, where ũ has the smooth germ supplied by H001; hence it is differentiable at z. For small real h, z+hT=(x0,tau+h) remains in Ω. The Fréchet differentiability expansion gives ũ(z+hT)=ũ(z)+hDũ(z)[T]+o(|h|), since ||hT||=|h|. This is precisely the one-variable derivative assertion. Regularity outside Ω is irrelevant.

background_notes.fact: For a scalar real function g with HasDerivAt g c tau, its real Fréchet derivative evaluated at 1 equals c; a constant real function has zero Fréchet derivative. Thus if the Fréchet derivatives of g and the constant 1 agree at tau, then c=0.

background_notes.justification: HasDerivAt g c tau means g(tau+h)=g(tau)+hc+o(|h|). This is the Fréchet expansion with continuous linear map h↦hc on ℝ; its value at 1 is c. Derivatives are unique: the difference of two such linear maps, evaluated on nonzero h and divided by h as h→0, must vanish at 1, and a real linear map ℝ→ℝ is determined by that value. A constant has zero increments and therefore the zero derivative. Applying the supplied M009 equality and evaluating at 1 consequently gives c=0.
